report.trigger: The third-party payment gateway had a burst of 503 errors. On checkout-api-3, payment_gateway_5xx_rate was 2.3% at 09:19:40Z, peaked at 87.0% at 09:21:00Z and was back to 0 at 09:21:40Z.
report.root_cause: Deploy dep-8841 (commit a3f9c2e, finished 09:14:47Z) changed the gateway retry policy in checkout/payment_client.py. It added 503 to status_forcelist, set allowed_methods=None (so POST charges are now retried) and set backoff_factor to 0. As a result, each failing POST /checkout made 4 gateway attempts, taking about 31 s. checkout-api holds its DB connection for the whole gateway call and every retry. So during the gateway burst, checkouts held connections long enough to fill the 15-connection pool on the instance for 76 seconds, and every endpoint then timed out waiting for a connection. Holding the connection across the gateway call is a necessary co-condition: the new retry policy only exhausts the pool because of it.
report.failure_mode: Customers on checkout-api-3 got generic 503s and very slow responses on every endpoint, not just checkout. In the replay of the deployed configuration there were 124 503s: 105 were the app's own pool timeouts after the 10 s pool_timeout, and 68 of all 503s were on read pages (/cart and /orders/{id}) that never call the gateway. The other 19 were gateway 503s passed through on POST /checkout after about 31 s of retries. checkout_5xx_rate peaked at 70.8%. Replay p95 latency was 40.6 s for POST /checkout and 10 s for reads.
contributing_factors: By design, checkout-api holds its DB connection through the gateway call and all its retries (runbook 'Connection handling contract'). Releasing the connection before the gateway call removed pool exhaustion in replay.
The pool is small (5 + 10 overflow = 15 per instance, pool_timeout=10 s) and all endpoints share it. Doubling it to 30 still saturated the pool for 14 s and raised read p95 to 807 ms.
backoff_factor=0 sends retries immediately at a gateway that is already failing.
allowed_methods=None retries POST charges, which are not idempotent. This is a double-charge risk, separate from the outage.
ruled_out: Gateway outage alone: rejected. With the gateway burst still present but the old retry policy restored, the replay had no pool timeouts, no read-page 503s and 0 s of pool saturation. Only 93 checkout POSTs failed with gateway 503s passed through, instead of an outage across all endpoints.

A cause inside checkout-api that doesn't depend on the gateway: rejected. With the burst removed and everything else as deployed, the replay had 0 503s and a checkout p95 of 226 ms. checkout_5xx_rate also returned to 0 at 09:21:35Z, before the gateway recovered, so there was no error tail after the gateway recovered.
CPU saturation: rejected. cpu_percent stayed at roughly 25–37% on the dashboard.
Pool too small as the root cause: rejected. At 30 connections the pool timeouts disappeared, but the pool still saturated for 14 s, so the long connection holds caused by retries remained the driver.
report.counterfactual_evidence: All replays used the same 5,576 requests. (1) Deployed configuration: 124 503s (105 pool timeouts, 19 gateway; 68 on reads), 76 s of pool saturation, 53 checkouts retried, checkout p95 40,568 ms, read p95 10,000 ms. This matches production: 105 pool-timeout and 19 gateway traces. (2) Old retry policy restored: 93 503s, all gateway 503s on checkout POSTs; 0 pool timeouts, 0 read 503s, 0 s saturated; checkout p95 11,125 ms, read p95 49 ms. (3) Gateway burst removed: 0 503s, checkout p95 226 ms. (4) DB connection released before the gateway call: 33 gateway 503s, 0 pool timeouts, 0 s saturated, read p95 49 ms, but checkout p95 still 37,938 ms because of retries. (5) pool_capacity=30: 33 gateway 503s, 0 pool timeouts, 14 s saturated, read p95 807 ms. Conclusion: reverting the retry policy alone prevents pool exhaustion and the outage across all endpoints. Checkout POSTs that hit the failing gateway still fail, which is the unavoidable part of the trigger.
report.documentation_evidence: None consulted. How the retry settings behave was taken from the diff and from the observed traces: req-01832 shows 4 POST attempts, all 503.
evidence_citations: dep-8841 diff, checkout/payment_client.py: '+ status_forcelist={502, 503, 504}', '+ allowed_methods=None', '+ backoff_factor=0' (previously {502,504}, {"GET"}, 0.5)
trace req-01832 POST /checkout, start 09:19:32.565Z: 4 payment_gateway.charge POST attempts, all 503 (8371, 6341, 6262 and 10380 ms); total 31384 ms; outcome 503_gateway
trace req-01884 GET /orders/{id}, start 09:19:46.716Z: db.acquire_connection 10000 ms timeout; outcome 503_pool_timeout
Runbook: pool_size=5, max_overflow=10, pool_timeout=10; connection held through the gateway call and its retries
report.remaining_uncertainty: Only checkout-api-3 was examined; the other five instances were not. The replays are a simulation and were not repeated in production. I did not check whether the immediate retries made the gateway's own error rate worse. I did not check whether retried POST charges caused duplicate charges. Even with the old policy, 93 checkouts failed during the gateway burst, so how checkout degrades under a gateway burst is still a separate issue.
report.recommended_fix: Immediately: roll back dep-8841 (kubectl rollout undo deployment/checkout-api), or restore status_forcelist={502,504}, allowed_methods={"GET"} and backoff_factor=0.5. Do not retry non-idempotent POST charges unless they carry idempotency keys. Next: release the DB connection before the gateway call and reacquire it to commit, or cap the total gateway time per request well below pool_timeout. Consider a separate pool for reads and a circuit breaker on the gateway. Audit 09:19–09:22 for duplicate charges from retried POSTs.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Gateway 503 burst (trigger) + dep-8841 retry policy (503 added, POST retried, backoff 0) with DB connection held across gateway call exhausted the 15-conn pool, causing pool-timeout 503s on all endpoints.
hypotheses.supporting_evidence: req-01832: 4 POST charge attempts, 31.4s holding conn. 105 503_pool_timeout traces (/orders 42, /checkout 37, /cart 26) vs 19 503_gateway. db_pool_in_use 15 from 09:19:50 to 09:21:00. Diff: status_forcelist adds 503, allowed_methods=None, backoff_factor=0.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Alternative: gateway outage alone explains the incident (no checkout-internal cause).
hypotheses.supporting_evidence: Rejection evidence: most 503s are pool timeouts on /cart and /orders which never call the gateway; checkout 503s ended at 09:21:35, not after gateway recovery, so no tail — needs replay to separate.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Root cause: the dep-8841 retry policy, which retries 503 POSTs 3x with no backoff, made each connection-holding checkout hold its connection much longer, which exhausted the 15-conn pool during the gateway burst. The connection-held design is a necessary co-condition.
hypotheses.supporting_evidence: Replays. Baseline: 124 503s (105 pool timeout, 68 on reads), 76s saturated. Revert retry: 0 pool timeouts, 0 read 503s, 0s saturated, 93 gateway 503s. Remove burst: 0 503s. Release connection before gateway: 0 pool timeouts, 33 gateway 503s. Pool 30: 0 pool timeouts but 14s saturated, read p95 807ms.
